```{r}
#| label: options

options(housepi.footer.warranty = TRUE)
```

Here we show how to compute common household measures according to the model posterior distribution. This is generally referred to as Posterior Predictive Checks (PPC) [@gelman_posterior_1996]. We use the same final-size example presented in [Get started](housepi.html):

```{r}
#| label: inference-setup
# repeat inference as in 'Get Started'
library(housepi)
set_housepi_theme()
set.seed(42)

hhmodel <- flu_1918_frederick |>
  new_housepi_model("final-size") |>
  add_parameter(import = "template")

# store posterior draws
results <- hhmodel |>
  run_inference()
```

# Predicted cases by size

We can use the simulation process to challenge the validity of the inferred model on top of the original dataset. We do so by computing the predicted numbers of cases per household size according to our posterior distribution (i.e. by producing simulations according to posterior values).

```{r}
#| label: compute-predictions
# compute posterior predictive checks
ppc <- hhmodel |>
  # run simulations according to previous posterior traces in results
  check_predictive(results)
print(ppc)
```

To show both observed and predicted cases by size, we can extract the formatted cases table from our output object as follows.

```{r}
#| label: format-cases-table
# for this part of the analysis we consider only house sizes up to 5
ppc$set_max_hhsize(5)

# return a data.frame with observed and predicted cases
cases_df <- ppc$formatted_cases_count

# format predicted cases
combined <- cases_df$predicted
mask_pred <- cases_df$predicted$distr == "predicted"
mask_cols <- setdiff(names(cases_df$predicted), c("hhsize", "distr"))

# format predicted values with their lower and upper credible interval bounds
combined[mask_pred, mask_cols] <- format_credible_interval(
  cases_df$predicted[mask_pred, mask_cols],
  cases_df$cri_lower[mask_pred, mask_cols],
  cases_df$cri_upper[mask_pred, mask_cols],
  as_integer = TRUE
)

# generate cases by household size table
flextable::flextable(combined) |>
  flextable::separate_header() |>
  flextable::bold(j = ~ hhsize, bold = TRUE) |>
  flextable::merge_v(j = ~ hhsize) |>
  flextable::align(align = "center", part = "all") |>
  flextable::labelizor(labels = c(hhsize = "Size",
                                  distr = "Distribution",
                                  cases = "Number of Cases")) |>
  flextable::autofit()
```

# Secondary attack rate

We can have a quick look at secondary attack rates of observed vs predicted cases as follows:

```{r}
#| label: sar-plot
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Secondary attack rates by household size comparing posterior estimates (orange) with observed data (black points with sample sizes).
#|  Predicted values show mean posterior estimates with 95% credible intervals, stratified by household size from 2 to 7 members.

# we drop maximum house size before proceeding
ppc$drop_max_hhsize()

library(ggplot2)

col_dict <- c(Predicted = "coral", Observed = "black")

# extract values for secondary attack rate
ggplot(ppc$formatted_sec_attack_rate,
       aes(x = as.factor(hhsize), y = observed,
           label = sprintf("[%s]", counts))) +
  # predicted SAR
  geom_point(aes(y = predicted, color = "Predicted")) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y = predicted, ymin = cri_lower, ymax = cri_upper,
                    color = "Predicted")) +
  # observed SAR
  geom_point(aes(color = "Observed")) +
  # annotate observed counts
  geom_text(nudge_x = 0.3, color = col_dict["Observed"]) +
  scale_color_manual(values = col_dict) +
  labs(x = "Household Size", y = "Secondary Attack Rate", color = "")
```

# Other posterior measures

`check_predictive()` also accepts named measure functions, computed on the simulated data and compared with the observed values.
They are checked alongside the standard epidemiological measures, so each needs a name of its own.
Current standard measures are stratified by household size:

- `measure_ar_by_hhsize`: attack rate;
- `measure_sar_by_hhsize`: secondary attack rate;
- `measure_cases_by_hhsize`: counts of cases.

`measure_geom_mean_hhsize` returns a single number instead: the geometric mean of household size weighted by secondary cases, a data-driven choice for `hhsize_ref`.

A custom measure function should accept a `data_wide` data.frame and return a `data.frame`, a `list`, or a `numeric` vector:
  
```{r}
#| label: predicted-measures-custom
# define a custom measure: overall attack rate
measure_overall_attack_rate <- function(data_wide) {
  sum(data_wide$status > 0, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(data_wide)
}

# compute standard and custom measures together
ppc_multi <- hhmodel |>
  check_predictive(results, overall = measure_overall_attack_rate)
ppc_multi
```

The returned `HousepiEpiPredictiveCheck` object stores `observed`, `predicted`, `cri_lower` and `cri_upper` for each measure, accessible by name:
  
```{r}
#| label: extract-sar-components
# bind observed secondary attack rates
ppc_multi$sec_attack_rate$observed |> 
  # to predicted (posterior mean) values
  dplyr::left_join(ppc_multi$sec_attack_rate$predicted, by = "hhsize", 
                   suffix = c("_observed", "_predicted"))
```

With `epi = FALSE` only the custom measures are checked.
The result is then a `HousepiPredictiveCheck` object, without the formatted outputs and the household size bounds of the standard check:

```{r}
#| label: predicted-measures-only-custom
hhmodel |>
  check_predictive(results, overall = measure_overall_attack_rate,
                   epi = FALSE)
```

Similarly can be done for all stored measures:

```{r}
#| label: plot-overall-attack-rate
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Overall attack rates comparison between observed and predicted.
#|  Predicted mean value shown with errorbars for the 95% credible interval
# compare observed vs predicted overall attack rate
ggplot(data.frame(ppc_multi$overall)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = "observed", y = observed), color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(x = "predicted", y = observed,
                    ymin = cri_lower, ymax = cri_upper)) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = "predicted", y = predicted)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attack rate")

```
